intro: Here's how to convert a string to title case in {lang}.
notes: Python's str.title() uppercases after any non-letter (so 'don't' -> 'Don'T'); use a regex or a library for smarter casing. JS has no built-in — split and map.

languages.python:
text = 'hello world, welcome to python'

# Built-in (note the apostrophe quirk):
print(text.title())   # Hello World, Welcome To Python
print("don't stop".title())   # Don'T Stop  (apostrophe quirk!)

# Word-aware capitalization:
def title_case(s: str) -> str:
    return ' '.join(w.capitalize() for w in s.split())

print(title_case(text))            # Hello World, Welcome To Python
print(title_case("don't stop"))   # Don't Stop

# str.capwords does the same:
import string
print(string.capwords(text))

intro: Here's how to extract all numbers from a string in {lang}.
notes: re.findall(r'\d+', s) grabs digit runs. Include decimals/negatives with a richer pattern like -?\d+(\.\d+)?.

languages.python:
import re

text = 'Order 42 costs 19.99 dollars, -3 in stock, id: 007'

# Integer runs:
print(re.findall(r'\d+', text))
# ['42', '19', '99', '3', '007']

# Decimals and negatives:
print(re.findall(r'-?\d+\.?\d*', text))
# ['42', '19.99', '-3', '007']

# As floats:
print([float(x) for x in re.findall(r'-?\d+\.?\d*', text)])

# Whole numbers only (not part of a larger number):
print(re.findall(r'\b\d+\b', text))

# Numbers >= some threshold:
print([int(x) for x in re.findall(r'\d+', text) if int(x) > 10])

intro: Here's a regex for matching hex color codes in {lang}.
notes: #RGB (3 digits) and #RRGGBB (6 digits) are both valid CSS hex colors — optionally with a trailing alpha (#RRGGBBAA). The boundary check avoids matching hex digits inside larger tokens.

languages.python:
import re

# 3 or 6 digits, case-insensitive:
HEX_COLOR = re.compile(r'#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}\b|#[0-9a-fA-F]{3}\b')

# Validate a single color:
def is_hex_color(s: str) -> bool:
    return bool(HEX_COLOR.fullmatch(s.strip()))

# Extract from text:
text = 'Use #ff0000 or #F00, and also #1a2b3c, but not #12345'
print(HEX_COLOR.findall(text))   # ['#ff0000', '#F00', '#1a2b3c']

print(is_hex_color('#fff'))      # True
print(is_hex_color('#ff0000'))   # True
print(is_hex_color('#ff00001'))  # False

# With optional alpha (#RRGGBBAA):
HEX_WITH_ALPHA = re.compile(r'#(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{6}|[0-9a-fA-F]{3})(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{2})?\b')

intro: Here's how to validate a YYYY-MM-DD date string in {lang}.
notes: Regex only checks the SHAPE — '2023-02-31' passes. Use a real date parser to validate calendar correctness (leap years, month lengths).

languages.python:
from datetime import datetime


def is_valid_date(date_str: str) -> bool:
    """True for real calendar dates in YYYY-MM-DD form."""
    try:
        datetime.strptime(date_str, '%Y-%m-%d')
        return True
    except ValueError:
        return False

# Shape check first (regex):
import re
shape_ok = re.fullmatch(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', date_str) is not None

# Examples:
print(is_valid_date('2023-02-28'))   # True
print(is_valid_date('2023-02-31'))   # False (Feb has 28/29 days)
print(is_valid_date('2023-13-01'))   # False (month 13)
print(is_valid_date('23-02-28'))     # False (wrong shape)

# Range-aware alternative:
def is_valid_iso(s: str) -> bool:
    import re as _re
    if not _re.fullmatch(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', s):
        return False
    y, m, d = map(int, s.split('-'))
    return 1 <= m <= 12 and 1 <= d <= 31

# Note: is_valid_iso('2023-02-31') is True — use strptime for full checks.

intro: Here's how to find a substring's position in {lang}.
notes: Python str.find returns -1 when absent; str.index raises ValueError. JS indexOf returns -1; use .search() with regexes. For repeated matches, use finditer (Python) or matchAll (JS).

languages.python:
text = 'the quick brown fox'

print(text.find('quick'))      # 4
print(text.find('zzz'))        # -1

# index() raises when absent:
try:
    print(text.index('quick'))
except ValueError:
    print('not found')

# Last occurrence:
print(text.rfind('o'))         # 15

# All occurrences:
def all_indexes(text: str, sub: str):
    start = 0
    while True:
        i = text.find(sub, start)
        if i == -1:
            return
        yield i
        start = i + 1

print(list(all_indexes('banana', 'na')))   # [2, 4]

# Case-insensitive:
print(text.lower().find('QUICK'.lower()))
